newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes leap on heating oil in short session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes leap on heating oil in short session.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes leaped in an abbreviated holiday session Tuesday afternoon, tracking the path of higher heating oil.
February West Texas Intermediate was pegged around $25.85-95 a barrel, up 55 cents from late Monday's cash market. The Feb/Mar WTI spread stood at 68 cents.
"Heat took everything up with it," one trader noted.

The market closed at 1300 EST/1800 GMT in observance of New Year's Eve, and will reopen for a regular session on January 2. Electronic Access trading will be closed tonight and will reopen at 1900 EST January 1/0000 GMT January 2.
Traders noted that low liquidity contributed to the run-up. "Things are very thin, so the market's easily pushed around," one said.
Grade business was moderate. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James changed hands at 32 cents, up one to two cents from this morning's dealings, but down four to nine cents from late Monday.
Domestic sweet grades are under pressure, not only from the open transatlantic arbitrage, but also from low refinery demand.
"There's a lack of demand due to extremely warm weather. Refining margins are awful," one market source said.
WTI/Midland was talked at minus two cts to flat, down slightly from late Monday, after trading earlier in the day at minus one cent.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet was dealt at a steady 20 cents premium to WTI/Cushing.

West Texas Sour/Midland was at WTI/Cushing minus $1.49-47 cents, up four cents on the buy side from Monday. A buying binge by a top U.S. refiner drove up sours, traders said. Deals were done at $1.49/1.48 a barrel.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was done at $2.50 a barrel, and rounded out the day in a range of $2.50-55 a barrel, up two cents on the offer side from Monday.
